requirement_text.ISS-0216: Letflow.Api.Pagination.decode_cursor/4 trusts its caller-supplied prefix with no non-empty guard, a real bypass path once REQ-072-onward endpoints call it. check_prefix/2 (lib/letflow/api/pagination.ex) uses a size guard (byte_size(decoded) >= byte_size(prefix) and String.starts_with?(decoded, prefix)) that trivially passes if prefix is an empty string, since every decoded cursor starts with the empty string -- an empty prefix defeats the cross-endpoint isolation this parameter exists to provide. Filed 2026-08-21 as unreachable-but-real-risk (REQ-072 routing layer was pending); NOW LIVE -- confirmed 2026-08-26 that real route handlers (lib/letflow/routers/audit.ex, tasks.ex, instances.ex, routers/tenants.ex, routers/identity.ex, definitions.ex) already call decode_cursor/4 with hardcoded non-empty module-attribute prefixes. The guard itself is still missing.

result.summary:
Re-read lib/letflow/design/iss0216-pagination-prefix-guard.md in full after rework 1/3 (git log shows commit f89b881 'design(ISS-0216): rework -- strip implementation code from §2.1', on top of the original b25798b). This is a re-validation focused on the single prior FAIL (check 5) plus a sanity re-check of the other five.

Check 5 (no implementation code) -- now PASSES. §2.1 no longer contains a literal `defp check_prefix(...)`/`do:`/`raise` Elixir clause. The only fenced code block in §2.1 is `@spec check_prefix(binary(), String.t()) :: :ok | {:error, :wrong_endpoint}` labeled 'unchanged' -- a type signature, which is exactly what CODE-DESIGNER's charter permits ('signatures and type shapes only'). The new clause itself is now described entirely in prose: its match pattern ('second argument is the empty string, disregarding the first argument entirely'), its dispatch position ('added immediately above the existing clause... Elixir clause dispatch tries clauses top-to-bottom'), its effect ('raises ArgumentError... does not return :ok or {:error, ...} -- execution does not fall through to a return value at all'), and an itemized list of what the exception message must convey (four bullet points: which function was misused, what the precondition is, why it matters, and a pointer to the new INV-9 invariant) rather than a literal finished message string. §2.2 similarly only restates decode_cursor/4's existing @spec (also 'unchanged') and describes in prose that no guard is added on decode_cursor/4's own head and why. §0's quote of the *existing* check_prefix/2 body (lines 211-218, cited for diagnosis) is unchanged from the original and is correctly out of scope for this check (existing shipped code being cited, not new code being authored) -- consistent with the prior validator's own carve-out. I found no other Elixir code (no defp/def, no do:/end block, no literal raise/case/with clause) anywhere else in the document. Grepped the full file for `defp `, `do:`, `raise ArgumentError,` outside of prose quoting -- the only remaining occurrences are inside the §0 existing-code quote and prose sentences describing behavior (e.g. 'it raises ArgumentError' as a sentence, not a code line). Check 5 now passes.

Sanity re-check of the other five (all previously PASS, unchanged in substance per CODE-DESIGNER's own rework summary, verified independently rather than taken on trust):
1. Exact clause named -- still true: check_prefix/2 gains one new leading function-head clause matching prefix == ""; decode_cursor/4's with-chain and @spec stated unchanged. Same root cause as step-01 (lines 211-218).
2. Error-shape decision explicit -- still true: raise ArgumentError, §1 gives the full three-part rationale (why not reuse :wrong_endpoint, why not a new {:error, :invalid_prefix} tuple, why raising is INV-8-compliant since INV-8 is scoped to network-facing input per the moduledoc), flagged as overridable in §5 (disclosure, not deferral, not a TBD).
3. @spec deltas stated -- still true: both check_prefix/2's and decode_cursor/4's @spec are explicitly stated unchanged, with rationale (raise isn't part of an Elixir @spec return type).
4. TEST-DESIGNER scope named -- still true, §4: mandatory empty-prefix case (assert_raise ArgumentError), non-regression on the five existing return-value cases, an optional boundary-prefix case, and an explicit 'do not test check_prefix/2 directly, only through public decode_cursor/4' constraint.
6. Handoff mechanics -- step-02-code-designer.json's own handoff correctly names next_action 'Route to CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR', status COMPLETED.

No new TBD/deferral language introduced by the rework. Cross-module dependencies still correctly stated as none (owned_modules remains exactly lib/letflow/api/pagination.ex; no route-handler change). All six checks now pass -- gate clears.
